newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asians see dominant world role - survey.
newsitem.headline: Asians see dominant world role - survey.

text.p: Asians are generally confident the Asia Pacific region will be a dominant force in world politics and economics in the next century, a survey released on Wednesday found.
It said they also aspire to balance work and play, educate their children abroad, travel freely and own their homes.
The survey by MasterCard on Asian ideals showed that with the exception of Japan, most were confident the Asia Pacific would dominate in the next century.
Only 48 percent of Japanese believed the Asia Pacific region would be a dominant force, the lowest score in the region.
The survey sought views on a wide range of topics from emigration to education and polled 5,442 people in 13 countries, including Australia and New Zealand.
It said that those in predominantly ethnic Chinese countries ranked the making of as much money as possible during one's working life as among "things especially important".
Taiwan ranked first on this issue with 87 percent, Singapore second at 71 percent, and Hong Kong third at 68 percent.
A balance between work and leisure and being able to afford higher education for children were especially important.
The desire to have children educated abroad, however, varied greatly with Australia and New Zealand differing from other Asia Pacific countries.
In Australia, only eight percent wished to educate their children abroad, while in New Zealand the figure was 11 percent.
Attitudes in the north of Asia were acutely different, with 50 percent in Hong Kong and China wanting foreign educational opportunities for their children, the survey said.
On the issue of emigration, it found that with fewer than 80 days to Hong Kong's handover by Britain to China, only 15 percent of those polled said they planned to emigrate.

"The Hong Kong emigration figures, particularly when compared to the likes of Singapore, Korea and Japan, are very surprising indeed," Brian Thom, MasterCard International, Asia Pacific's senior vice-president for marketing, said.
The Hong Kong figure was below the average and compared with 33 percent of Filipinos and 19 percent of Singaporeans.
The survey said that to travel anywhere whenever one wished was selected by 66 percent of respondents.
This was followed by living in one's own house or apartment, which secured a score of 60 percent.
